publisher: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Student and Exchange Visitor Program
raw_extract: In 2004, Congress mandated all nonimmigrant students and exchange visitors must pay the I-901 SEVIS Fee, which funds the Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP) and SEVIS. This fee is separate from visa fees and school SEVIS administration fees. … Fee Amounts … I-901 SEVIS FeesDescriptionAmountI-901 SEVIS Fee F or M visa applicants (full payment)$350I-901 SEVIS Fee J visa applicants (full payment)$220I-901 SEVIS Fee special J-visa categories (subsidized payment)$35I-901 SEVIS Fee government visitor (no payment)$0
research_notes: This is the federally mandated SEVIS fee for F and M applicants, published by ICE itself. It is explicitly separate from the Department of State visa application fee. The Department of State M-visa application fee could not be verified: travel.state.gov returned HTTP 403 to every request, so the commonly cited USD 185 MRV application fee is deliberately NOT recorded here as a claim. The I-901 figure is the only US student visa-related fee I personally fetched. The page's footer shows 'Updated: 12/10/2024'; the 2026 as_of reflects retrieval year because the page carries no effective date for the amounts.

claims.statement: ICE charges F or M visa applicants a mandatory I-901 SEVIS fee of USD 350, separate from visa fees and school SEVIS administration fees.
